# B295 — NAME COLLISIONS in a `[service]`/`[client_service]` expansion, B282's family not closed: an `[rpc]` method named `call` fails the build ("in code generated by this attribute: `call` expects 2 arguments, but got 4", spanned on the STRUCT) because the generated `<Name>Client` stub calls the imported FREE `call(self.transport, self.codec, ..)` from inside an impl that now declares `fun call`; a `[client_service]` method named `notify` fails the same way through `<Name>Proxy`; and `__request` (B282's gensym) is now the reserved parameter name — an `[rpc]` parameter literally named `__request` reproduces B282

- status: OPEN — Order 32's finds (2026-09-11)
- kind: bug
- area: Reactive core & UI

Two fixes, pick one per name: QUALIFY the free calls in generated stubs (`rpc::call(..)`, `rpc::notify(..)` — the import list at rpc.vl ~4993 is where the unqualified names come from) so a user method of the same name cannot shadow them; or REFUSE the colliding names at the attribute in the method's vocabulary (one row, two names + the `__` prefix). Qualifying is the honest fix (it removes the hazard instead of naming it); the `__` prefix is a refusal either way (a user cannot be asked to know the generator's bindings). Pins: `[rpc] fun call(self, what: str): str` round-trips; `[client_service] fun notify(self, what: str)` round-trips; `[rpc] fun f(self, __request: str)` refused.
